Side A · Recipe 06

Three against four

Polyrhythmic echo groove

A bass in plain 4/4 and an echo that only knows threes. The two cycles cross and meet again every bar, and a simple blip becomes a groove.

Level
Medium
Setup
15 min
Key
E minor
  1. What you'll hear
  2. 1. PERfourMER: a short blip and a bass
  3. 2. Grand Canyon: a three-head drum echo
  4. 3. NightSky: a small, tight room

What you'll hear

The bass thumps four times a bar. A short blip plays once, and the echo answers it three times, evenly spread across the same bar. Three against four: it feels like the groove is turning over itself.

The trick: the Grand Canyon's DRUM echo spreads its echoes over the delay time, one per playback head. Its secondary mode uses three heads instead of four.

1. PERfourMER: a short blip and a bass

Synth channel 1 (MIDI 1) is the blip; channel 2 (MIDI 2) is the bass, out of its own jack. Channels 3 and 4 VOLUME down.

  • 1Ch 1 WAVEsinetrianglesquaresawnoiseEXTA woody blip.
  • 2Ch 1 OCTAVE4'High, so it cuts through.
  • 3Ch 1 CUTOFF1 o'clockBright.
  • 4Ch 1 RESONANCE11 o'clockA resonant ping.
  • 5Ch 1 ATTACKminInstant.
  • 6Ch 1 DECAY9 o'clockVery short: a blip.
  • 7Ch 1 SUSTAINminNothing held.
  • 8Ch 1 RELEASEminClean stop: the echo pattern stays crisp.
  • 9Ch 2 WAVEsinetrianglesquaresawnoiseEXTA full bass.
  • 10Ch 2 OCTAVE16'Low.
  • 11Ch 2 CUTOFF10 o'clockRound.
  • 12Ch 2 Filter EG INT1 o'clockA little punch on each note.
  • 13Ch 2 DECAY10 o'clockShort, so the four beats are clear.
  • 14Ch 2 SUSTAIN10 o'clockA little body. Everything else on channel 2: the bass patch from the rig page.

2. Grand Canyon: a three-head drum echo

  • 1DELAY TYPEDRUMA magnetic drum echo: the delay time is split evenly between its playback heads.
  • Secondary modeHold PING PONG about 2 s, until the DRUM LED blinks, then let goThree heads instead of four: rhythms in threes.
  • 2RHYTHM (left mini knob)Step 7 of 8: heads 1, 2 and 3All three heads play: three even echoes. Count the positions from fully left.
  • 3DRUM AGE (right mini knob)11 o'clockA bit of age: darker, slightly distorted, warbling.
  • TAP DIVPress until only the quarter LED lightsSo the tapped time is used as is.
  • TempoTap the TAP/LOOP footswitch once per bar, on the bar's first beatThe delay time becomes one whole bar, so its three heads land evenly across it: three against the bass's four.
  • 4FEEDBACK9 o'clockMostly one pass: the pattern stays clear.
  • 5DELAY LVLnoonEchoes as loud as they need to be heard.

3. NightSky: a small, tight room

  • 1TEXTUREsparsedensediffuseA fast, dense plate.
  • 2LENGTH10 o'clockShort, so the rhythm stays tight.
  • 3SIZE/PITCH11 o'clockA smaller space (clockwise makes it bigger).
  • 4FILTERregenlow passSimple tone control.
  • 5HIGH CUT1 o'clockA little soft.
  • 6LOW CUTnoonNo low end in the reverb at all.
  • 7SHIMMER (knob)minOff.
  • 8GLIMMERhighlowoffOff.
  • 9DEPTHminNo modulation.
  • 10DRYnoonUnity.
  • 11REVERB10 o'clockJust a little air.

4. The OXI One: play it

  1. Tempo 90–100 BPM. Not slower than about 85: one bar must fit in the delay's 3-second maximum.
  2. Sequencer 1 (Mono, Ch 1): one blip on step 1. Short gate.
  3. Sequencer 2 (Mono, Ch 2): a low E on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four on the floor.
  4. Tap the Grand Canyon's TAP/LOOP once on each bar's first beat, two bars in a row.

You got it right when

  • Count the bass 1-2-3-4: the three echoes land between its beats, and meet it again on beat 1.

5. The performance

  • Turn RHYTHM to other positions: some play two of the three heads, for lopsided patterns.
  • Leave secondary mode (hold PING PONG again) and turn RHYTHM to position 4: four heads, a plain echo on every beat, and suddenly everything lines up with the bass. Switch back and forth for tension and release. (In standard mode the RHYTHM positions pick different rhythms.)

If it sounds wrong

  • Echoes land on the bass beats: you're in standard (four-head) mode, or the delay isn't one bar. Re-tap once per bar.
  • The tap won't stretch to a bar: the delay tops out at 3 seconds, so below about 85 BPM a bar is too long. Speed up, or tap half a bar and hear it as three against two.

Sources

  • Grand Canyon manual: DRUM, the rhythm table and "the delay time is divided by total number of drum playheads" (p. 21), secondary mode (p. 34), TAP DIV (p. 12).
  • NightSky manual: dense texture (p. 5), LOW CUT (p. 4).
  • PERfourMER MKII manual: filter and envelope (pp. 12–20), individual outputs (p. 21).
  • OXI One MKII manual: steps and gates (pp. 51, 55).
